subject: Post-demo: Model shortlist & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 26 Feb 2026 15:04:00 -0800
Subject: Post-demo: Model shortlist & next steps

Hi Jordan / Alicia —

Thanks again for taking the demo today. Great conversation — we captured your main constraints: tight latency target for chat (<200ms p95), strict cost targets for per-API call economics, and high quality on domain-specific product description generation (few-shot prompts).

Below is a short recommended model shortlist tailored to Acme's use case along with rationale and tradeoffs. I attached the prompt set we used for the quick eval and a short benchmark summary; Vivek included the detailed perf numbers in a follow-up.

Recommended shortlist (priority order):
1) redwood-instruct-7b-optim (recommended baseline)
   - Rationale: Best balance of output quality vs cost for your 512-token average outputs. Strong instruction-following on product description prompts.
   - Tradeoffs: p95 latency ~120-160ms on our dedicated pool; cost ~0.6x of larger models.

2) openx-13b-quant (high-quality option)
   - Rationale: Higher semantic fidelity for nuanced product copy; fewer hallucinations on catalog attributes. Good for pages that need high polish.
   - Tradeoffs: Higher cost (~1.8x) and higher p95 latency (~260-320ms) unless you accept a slightly higher latency SLO or move to Dedicated with 80% GPU headroom.

3) redwood-3.5-small-fast (cost-first option)
   - Rationale: Extremely low token cost and fast latencies (p95 <90ms) for short responses — good for scaled low-stakes endpoints (e.g., micro-copy and recommendations).
   - Tradeoffs: Lower creativity and occasional brevity; not recommended where subtle wording matters.

Next steps I suggest:
- Quick eval: we run the supplied prompt set (attached) against the three models and produce a one-page quality + perf summary.
- Agreement on SLAs: confirm your target p95 latency and preferred cost envelope so we can tune batching/quantization.
- If you want, we can run a 48-hour production pilot on your ingestion of ~50k requests/day to measure real-world economics.

Attachments: acme_eval_prompts.txt, benchmark_summary_acme.pdf

Would next Wednesday (Mar 4) at 10am PT work for a follow-up to review the short eval?

Thanks,
Marissa

Subject: Re: Post-demo: Model shortlist & next steps

Hi Jordan — quick answers, plus links to the short benchmark we ran: 

1) Availability: redwood-instruct-7b-optim is available on Hosted API now and also as a Dedicated pool image. Hosted has default concurrency limits (we can raise those during the pilot).

2) Hallucination examples: see the attached prompt-set outputs ("acme_eval_prompts.txt") and the benchmark PDF. In short: 7b-optim produced fewer invented product attributes on attribute-completion prompts. Example (from prompt 05):

On Wed, 26 Feb 2026 at 15:04:00 -0800, Marissa Cole wrote:
> Prompt: "Write a short description for a water-resistant travel backpack with laptop sleeve and TSA lock."
>
> redwood-instruct-7b-optim: "A durable, water-resistant travel backpack featuring a padded laptop sleeve that fits up to 15-inch laptops and an integrated TSA-friendly lock for secure airport screening. Ideal for business travelers."
>
> redwood-3.5-small-fast: "A lightweight backpack with a compartment for a laptop and a lock. Some models may include RFID protection."

The 3.5 variant added "RFID protection" in a couple of examples where it wasn't in the source prompt or catalog — that's the sort of hallucination we flagged. Full side-by-side examples are in the Drive link.

3) Cost math: At ~350 tokens, redwood-instruct-7b-optim sits around $0.008–$0.012 per call depending on batching. With conservative batching assumptions it should be within your $0.01 target for Hosted if we enable prefix caching and 2-4 request batch windows. If you need deterministic sub-0.01 per call we can model Dedicated pricing (committed throughput).

Benchmarks and links: 
- Short perf report (PDF): https://drive.example.com/file/d/benchmark_summary_acme.pdf
- Full eval artifacts (prompt outputs + scripts): https://drive.example.com/folder/acme-evals
- Simple perf chart (p95 latency vs model): https://dash.redwoodinference.com/reports/acme-p95-chart

I'll join the Mar 4 slot to walk through perf tradeoffs and the caching/batching knobs.

— Vivek
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
